text: Setting clear goals is the foundation of any successful project. A useful way to do this is by using SMART goals, which means your objectives are Specific, Measurable, Achievable, Relevant, and Time-bound. For example, instead of saying "improve the website," you might say "increase page speed by 20% within three months." Once your goals are set, you should break the work into smaller milestones, or checkpoints, to track progress. Each milestone should have clear deliverables, such as a report or a prototype. Finally, it is essential to ensure stakeholder alignment. This means regularly communicating with everyone involved, like clients or team members, so that everyone agrees on the direction and expectations. With clear goals and good communication, your project has a much higher chance of success.
